tas.helpUnified: One rule: with a selection the action applies to the selection (Delete clears it, the run-length box resizes it, copy / cut / paste), otherwise it applies to the current frame. Mouse mode 1 select / 2 fill / 3 key fill / 4 insert/remove; Alt+drag, Space / middle-drag, wheel zoom and W / S / A / D work in every mode.

helpRows.save: Save / Save as… (backs up to .tas.bak first)
helpRows.recordKeys: Key fill mode: replace the current frame (or the whole selection) with the keys you're holding; hold several for a combo (locked tracks unchanged)
helpRows.playCursor: Play from the editor's current frame (earlier frames fast-forward)
helpRows.playSpeed: Playback slower / faster (one step per press, works during playback)
helpRows.frames: Insert/Remove mode: left-drag = insert that many frames before the start (filled with the start frame's keys), right-drag = remove those frames (applied on release, all tracks shift together)
helpRows.menu: Select / key fill mode: context menu (copy, paste, insert frames left / right, remove frames…; inside the selection it uses the selection's frames, new frames copy the selection's start frame)
helpRows.modes: Mouse mode: 1 select (default) / 2 fill / 3 key fill / 4 insert/remove (also switchable above the timeline)
helpRows.pickRun: Select mode: click a run to select that whole run at once
helpRows.boxSelect: Select mode: drag inside one row to box-select part of that run (no cross-row, snapped to the pressed frames)
helpRows.fill: Fill mode: drag a rectangle — left sets every cell, right clears every cell (committed on release, one undo step)
helpRows.select: Key fill mode: drag out a time range (spans all tracks) — mapped keys replace the whole selection in one go
helpRows.row: Fill mode: only the starting row is changed
helpRows.move: Grab a contiguous block and drag it (can change track)
helpRows.zoom: Zoom in / out (hold for continuous, anchored on the pointer)
helpRows.wheelV: Scroll up / down; Ctrl + wheel = zoom (anchored on the pointer)
helpRows.view: Hold and drag = temporarily pan the view
helpRows.tab: Next / previous frame; with a selection, shift the whole range by one frame
helpRows.jumpRun: Jump to the previous / next run edge (Shift = extend the selection too)
helpRows.home: Jump to the first / last frame
helpRows.clear: Clear the selection; with no selection, clear the keys on the current frame
helpRows.esc: Cancel the selection and the current drag (a fill key in key fill mode)
helpRows.reorder: Drag up/down to reorder the tracks
helpRows.lock: Click the lock icon on a track header to lock / unlock that track

tas.helpRecord: Key fill mode: drag out a selection (or use the current frame), then ↑ ← → ↓ Shift Space Q Enter Esc become fill keys — each press replaces that range with the keys you're holding at that moment (hold several for a combo); Tab / Shift+Tab move the cursor, or shift a whole selection by one frame. Other modes ignore these keys.
tas.helpSelect: Select mode: click to select a whole run (an empty cell gives an empty selection of length 0); drag inside the row to box part of it; Alt+drag moves it (overwriting what is there), and the run-length box changes its frames — 0 deletes it, > 0 on an empty selection creates a key there.
tas.helpRunLength: Run-length box: only usable in select mode with a single-track selection. Edits apply live (each edit is one undo step).
tas.helpCover: Replace semantics (key fill mode): each press replaces the keys of every unlocked track in the selection (or current frame) with the keys you're holding — nothing accumulates: press ↑, release, press → and you get only →; for ↑+→ hold ↑ and press →. Locked tracks are not changed.
tas.helpLock: Track lock: a locked track is fully read-only — filling, recording, Alt-dragging, deleting a selection and pasting all skip it (inserting / deleting whole frames edits the timeline itself, so locked tracks shift too). Locks are remembered.
tas.helpPlayback: Playback (Playback panel): Play starts watching at the editor's current frame — earlier frames still run their physics but aren't rendered or paced, so they fast-forward; From start begins at frame 0. The speed slider can be changed any time during playback (applies on the next frame; the rightmost stop is unlimited). The game is view-only by default: clicks pass through to the editor and it can't capture the mouse; turn on Control the game when you need to send it keys (BallanceTAS F4–F8, stop key). After you stop, the game exits or you close the editor, the BallanceTAS settings changed by one-click play are restored automatically.
tas.helpBackup: Auto backup: before overwriting an existing .tas, the original is copied to <file>.tas.bak next to it (an older .bak is replaced). A failed backup never blocks saving.
tas.helpModes: Mouse modes (above the timeline or 1/2/3/4): Select = click a run to select it, drag inside a row to box-select part of it, run length edits its frames (0 = delete, > 0 on an empty cell = create); Fill = drag a rectangle, left sets every cell in it, right clears them; Key fill = drag a range, then press keys to replace it; Insert/Remove = left-drag inserts frames (filled with the start frame's keys), right-drag removes frames. Alt+drag, Space / middle-drag, wheel zoom and W / S / A / D work in every mode.
tas.helpRow: Single-row constraint: in fill mode, hold Shift while dragging and only the starting row is changed — moving vertically into other tracks never writes them.
tas.bandsHint: Show or hide the alternating background of each major tick interval (independent of the V-lines)
tas.mode: Mouse mode (1 select / 2 fill / 3 key fill / 4 insert/remove)
tas.modeSelectHint: Select: click a run to select the whole run; drag inside one row to box-select part of it; use the run-length box to resize it or create a key; Alt+drag moves it.
tas.modeFillHint: Fill: drag a rectangle, release left to set the whole block, right to clear it (one undo step).
tas.runLengthHint: After selecting a run you can edit its frame count: 0 deletes it; on an empty cell a value above 0 creates a key there.
